editions.summary: IOAI 2026 was a punishing break for contestants expecting something like IOAI 2025. Every task was genuinely hammer resistant (unable to be solved with off-the-shelf methods), as the IOAI Call for Tasks puts it: every Day 1 task shifted sharply from its at-home counterpart, while Day 2 offered no universal source of points. Most leading contestants combined strong scores on two tasks with at least 25 points on another two or three. This problem-specific style will probably define future editions.
taskCommentary: Already entirely different from the at-home task. Many high scorers found an exploitable property of the metric and implemented a trivial solution instead of using the provided model.
The closest to its at-home counterpart and the easiest direction to anticipate, although it demanded substantial manual preprocessing before the model could be used.
A challenging, non-trivial transformation of the at-home task.
Perhaps the clearest textbook example of its underlying method, though the implementation could still be difficult.
Harder than it first appeared to many contestants: unlike Task 1, many attempts that avoided the provided model failed badly.
One of the most gamified tasks. Extremely simple solutions could earn solid middle-range scores, but very few contestants scored highly.

editions.summary: The first IOAI with individual rounds. Day 1 developed the at-home task ideas to varying degrees, while Day 2 was markedly harder. The leading contestants generally secured strong scores on at least four tasks.
taskCommentary: Extremely close to the at-home task and an essential source of points.
A moderate shift, though important similarities with the at-home task remained.
A very challenging and relatively drastic evolution, albeit one that looked foreseeable in hindsight.
The hardest task: only three contestants scored at least 50 points.
Allowed a large score gain in very little time.
Very hard. Many high scorers used a highly optimized straightforward approach instead of the more complex intended solution.
